title: Pylon Side Link Fitting Lug — Oversize Bush Repair
abstract: Shop repair of a fretted or scored side link fitting lug bore by machining to the first oversize and fitting an oversize bush.

sections.purpose: This repair restores a side link fitting lug bore that has been fretted or scored beyond the acceptance limit, by machining to the first oversize and fitting an oversize bush.
sections.damage_assessment: This repair is done in the shop with the fitting off the aircraft. Measure the bore with a three-point gauge at three axial positions and record every reading. The repair is valid where the maximum material removal to clean up the bore does not exceed 0.6 mm on diameter and where no indication is found by fluorescent penetrant after clean-up. A bore that needs more than 0.6 mm, a bore with an indication after clean-up, or a lug with any crack in the surrounding land is scrap.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the existing bush by pressing it out on the bench with the fitting supported on the flange, never on the lug. Clean the bore and do a fluorescent penetrant inspection. Machine the bore to the first oversize dimension given on the repair drawing, holding the surface finish and the perpendicularity called out there. Do a second fluorescent penetrant inspection after machining and confirm that no indication remains. Chill the oversize bush and press it into the bore in one movement, checking the interference against the recorded bore reading. Ream the bush bore to the final dimension and check it with the plug gauge. Apply the surface protection of the standard practice to the exposed lug faces. Where the inboard lug D5450125058936 has been disturbed during removal, check its faying face for fretting before the fitting goes back on the aircraft, and renew the fairing screws AES177340K7.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a fluorescent penetrant inspection of the lug bore at the next engine shop visit after the repair. Report the repair to Aeralis with the bore readings before and after machining. A repaired bore that frets again is outside the scope of this scheme and the fitting must be referred to Aeralis.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Fretting or scoring that cleans up within 0.6 mm on diameter, with no penetrant indication after clean-up and no crack in the surrounding lug land.

title: Pylon Side Link Fitting Lug — Oversize Bush Repair

issue.reason: Fitting standard named, a single oversize declared and a reduced life limit with its recording rule added so that the repair is bounded against the tracked life.

abstract: Shop repair of a fretted or scored side link fitting lug bore on the aluminium interference-fit standard, by machining to the first oversize and fitting an oversize bush, with the reduced life limit that goes with it.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the lug bore of the aluminium side link fitting D5450125251057 that has been fretted or scored beyond the acceptance limit, by machining to the first oversize and fitting an oversize bush. The fitting is a life-limited part and this repair reduces that life, so it may only be embodied where the life record can be amended at the same time.
sections.damage_assessment: This repair is done in the shop with the fitting off the aircraft. Confirm the fitting standard from the part number stamped next to the serial number before anything else: this scheme is written for the aluminium interference-fit fitting only. Measure the bore with a three-point gauge at three axial positions and record every reading. The repair is valid where the maximum material removal to clean up the bore does not exceed 0.6 mm on diameter and where no indication is found by fluorescent penetrant after clean-up. A bore that needs more than 0.6 mm, a bore with an indication after clean-up, or a lug with any crack in the surrounding land is scrap. There is no second oversize: a fitting already at the first oversize cannot be repaired again.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the existing bush by pressing it out on the bench with the fitting supported on the flange, never on the lug. Clean the bore and do a fluorescent penetrant inspection. Machine the bore to the first oversize dimension given on the repair drawing, holding the surface finish and the perpendicularity called out there. Do a second fluorescent penetrant inspection after machining and confirm that no indication remains. Chill the oversize bush and press it into the bore in one movement, checking the interference against the recorded bore reading. Ream the bush bore to the final dimension and check it with the plug gauge. Apply the surface protection of the standard practice to the exposed lug faces. Mark the fitting with the oversize identifier next to its serial number and amend the life record before the fitting leaves the shop. Where the inboard lug D5450125058936 has been disturbed during removal, check its faying face for fretting before the fitting goes back on the aircraft, and renew the fairing screws AES177340K7.
sections.inspection_requirements: A fitting repaired to the first oversize carries a reduced life limit of 18 000 flight cycles from the date of repair, which replaces the original 24 000 flight cycle limit and must be entered in the life-limited parts record before the fitting leaves the shop. The oversize identifier is stamped next to the serial number so that the reduced limit cannot be lost if the paperwork is separated from the part. Do a fluorescent penetrant inspection of the lug bore at every engine shop visit rather than the general visual check applied to an unrepaired fitting. Report the repair to Aeralis with the bore readings before and after machining.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Fretting or scoring that cleans up within 0.6 mm on diameter, with no penetrant indication after clean-up and no crack in the surrounding lug land.

title: Pylon Side Link Fitting Lug — Oversize Bush Repair

issue.reason: Oversize scheme re-cut for the steel lug and the two variants published under separate effectivity, each with its own oversize dimension and reduced life.

abstract: Shop repair of a fretted or scored side link fitting lug bore, in two variants under separate effectivity — one for the aluminium interference-fit fitting and one for the high-strength steel four-bolt fitting — each with its own oversize dimension and reduced life limit.

sections.purpose: This repair restores a side link fitting lug bore that has been fretted or scored beyond the acceptance limit, by machining to the first oversize and fitting an oversize bush. Two variants are published. Variant 1 applies to the aluminium interference-fit fitting D5450125251057 of the pre MOD-162044 standard. Variant 2 applies to the high-strength steel four-bolt fitting XAN117135-98 of the post MOD-162044 standard. Both fittings are life-limited parts and each variant reduces that life by its own amount.
sections.damage_assessment: This repair is done in the shop with the fitting off the aircraft. Confirm the fitting standard from the part number stamped next to the serial number and select the variant accordingly; the two variants are not interchangeable and neither dimension transfers to the other lug. Measure the bore with a three-point gauge at three axial positions and record every reading. Variant 1 is valid where the maximum material removal to clean up the bore does not exceed 0.6 mm on diameter, which is set by the aluminium lug wall thickness. Variant 2 is valid to 0.4 mm on diameter: the steel lug wall is thinner for the same bore and the residual stress field left by machining reaches further into the land, so the aluminium figure is not conservative on it. In both variants a bore that needs more than the stated removal, a bore with a penetrant indication after clean-up, or a lug with any crack in the surrounding land is scrap. There is no second oversize in either variant.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the existing bush by pressing it out on the bench with the fitting supported on the flange, never on the lug. Clean the bore and do a fluorescent penetrant inspection. Machine the bore to the first oversize dimension of the selected variant as given on the repair drawing, holding the surface finish and the perpendicularity called out there; the steel variant is machined wet and at the reduced feed stated on sheet 2, because a dry cut leaves a white layer that the penetrant inspection will not find. Do a second fluorescent penetrant inspection after machining and confirm that no indication remains. Chill the oversize bush of the selected variant and press it into the bore in one movement, checking the interference against the recorded bore reading. Ream the bush bore to the final dimension and check it with the plug gauge. Apply the surface protection of the standard practice to the exposed lug faces. Mark the fitting with the oversize identifier and the variant number next to its serial number and amend the life record before the fitting leaves the shop. Where the interface plate D5450124639244 or the inboard lug D5450125058936 has been disturbed during removal, check the faying faces for fretting before the fitting goes back on the aircraft, and renew the fairing screws AES177340K7.
sections.inspection_requirements: A fitting repaired under variant 1 carries a reduced life limit of 18 000 flight cycles from the date of repair in place of 24 000. A fitting repaired under variant 2 carries a reduced life limit of 40 000 flight cycles in place of 60 000; the reduction is proportionally larger than variant 1 because the steel lug takes no benefit from the residual compression that cold expansion leaves in the aluminium. In both cases the reduced limit must be entered in the life-limited parts record before the fitting leaves the shop, and the variant number is stamped next to the serial number so that the limit cannot be lost with the paperwork. Do a fluorescent penetrant inspection of the lug bore at every engine shop visit rather than the general visual check applied to an unrepaired fitting. Report the repair to Aeralis with the bore readings before and after machining.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Variant 1, aluminium fitting: clean-up within 0.6 mm on diameter. Variant 2, steel fitting: clean-up within 0.4 mm on diameter. Either variant: no penetrant indication after clean-up and no crack in the surrounding lug land.
